materials.name: Custer Feldspar
materials.description: Potash feldspar, common flux for mid to high fire glazes. Discontinued 2024; its usual substitute G-200 HP is also discontinued, so Mahavir or a potash/soda feldspar blend is the practical route. Post-2021 datasheets show higher Na2O (4.5%).

materials.name: G-200 Feldspar
materials.description: Potash feldspar, slightly different from Custer

materials.name: Nepheline Syenite
materials.description: High-alkali flux, good for lowering maturing temperature

materials.name: Silica (Flint)
materials.description: Pure silica, glass former

materials.name: EPK Kaolin
materials.description: Edgar Plastic Kaolin, primary kaolin for glazes

materials.name: Grolleg Kaolin
materials.description: English kaolin, very white, good for porcelain

materials.name: Whiting (Calcium Carbonate)
materials.description: Primary calcium source, high temperature flux

materials.name: Wollastonite
materials.description: Calcium silicate, no LOI, reduces crazing

materials.name: Talc
materials.description: Magnesium silicate, promotes satin/matte surfaces

materials.name: Dolomite
materials.description: Calcium magnesium carbonate, promotes buttery matte

materials.name: Zinc Oxide
materials.description: Secondary flux, promotes crystal growth

materials.name: Gerstley Borate
materials.description: Natural calcium borate, primary boron source (variable)

materials.name: Frit 3134
materials.description: Calcium borate frit, lead-free, food safe

materials.name: Frit 3110
materials.description: Sodium silicate frit, high expansion

materials.name: Frit 3195
materials.description: Calcium borate frit, lower alkali than 3134

materials.name: Barium Carbonate
materials.description: Barium source, promotes matte, NOT food safe

materials.name: Strontium Carbonate
materials.description: Strontium source, safer alternative to barium

materials.name: Lithium Carbonate
materials.description: Powerful flux, promotes copper blues

materials.name: Spodumene
materials.description: Lithium feldspar, lower expansion flux

materials.name: Soda Ash
materials.description: Sodium carbonate, soluble flux — migrates to surface during drying

materials.name: Ball Clay (OM4)
materials.description: Old Mine #4, highly plastic ball clay

materials.name: Bentonite
materials.description: Plasticizer, use 1-2% maximum

materials.name: Alumina Hydrate
materials.description: Pure alumina source, increases viscosity

materials.name: Calcined Alumina
materials.description: Calcined alumina, no LOI

materials.name: Red Art
materials.description: Red iron-bearing earthenware clay, commonly used as a colorant in clay bodies and slips

materials.name: Hawthorne Bond
materials.description: Dark-burning fireclay with high iron content, used in stoneware bodies and as a slip material

materials.name: Ferro Frit 3124
materials.description: Calcium borate frit with higher alumina than 3134, good for cone 06-6

materials.name: Ferro Frit 3249
materials.description: Strontium-containing frit, used as a safer alternative to barium frits

materials.name: Gillespie Borate
materials.description: Gerstley Borate substitute with more consistent chemistry. Natural calcium borate source.

materials.name: Petalite
materials.description: Lithium aluminum silicate, low thermal expansion, used in flameware and ovenware bodies

materials.name: Pearl Ash (Potassium Carbonate)
materials.description: Soluble potassium source, migrates to surface during drying — used in ash glaze substitutions and some specialized glazes

materials.name: Volcanic Ash
materials.description: Natural volcanic glass, variable composition, can serve as both flux and silica source

materials.name: Wood Ash (Mixed Hardwood)
materials.description: Washed mixed hardwood ash, primary flux in traditional ash glazes. Composition varies by wood species.

materials.name: Rice Hull Ash
materials.description: High silica ash from rice hulls, used in nuka and other traditional Asian glazes

materials.name: Bone Ash (Calcium Phosphate)
materials.description: Tricalcium phosphate from calcined animal bones. Essential for bone china bodies and promotes opalescence in glazes.

materials.name: Pyrophyllite
materials.description: Aluminum silicate mineral, low thermal expansion, used in whiteware and low-expansion bodies

materials.name: Mullite
materials.description: 3Al2O3-2SiO2, refractory aluminum silicate formed at high temperature. Used in kiln furniture and refractory bodies.

materials.name: Magnesium Carbonate
materials.description: Pure magnesium source, promotes matte surfaces and crawling when used in excess. Light powder form.

materials.name: Alberta Slip
materials.description: Replacement for discontinued Albany Slip. Iron-bearing low-melting clay blend. Standalone glaze at cone 10R (chocolate brown gloss); use with frit at cone 6. Over 40% raw requires calcined/raw blend to prevent drying cracks.

materials.name: Alberta Slip Calcined
materials.description: Calcined version of Alberta Slip. Same chemistry but zero LOI and no shrinkage. Mixed with raw Alberta Slip (50/50 typical) in high-slip recipes to prevent drying cracks.

materials.name: Albany Slip
materials.description: Historic high-iron silty clay mined in Albany, NY — discontinued. Melted to glossy chocolate brown at cone 8-10R. Alberta Slip is the standard replacement.

materials.name: Minspar 200
materials.description: Soda feldspar from Spruce Pine, NC. Formerly NC-4 Feldspar; very similar to discontinued F-4. High Na2O raises thermal expansion — prone to crazing at high percentages.

materials.name: Cornwall Stone
materials.description: Complex low-iron feldspar from Cornwall, UK. Higher silica than most feldspars with diverse fluxes. Variable batch chemistry; often replaced by synthetic equivalents. Good for engobes and low-shrinkage glazes. Analysis excludes fluorine.

materials.name: Colemanite
materials.description: Natural calcium borate mineral. Very high B2O3 content — insoluble boron source. High concentrations cause decrepitation (wrinkling/spalling). Industry prefers boron frits; colemanite chemistry varies by source (Turkey, Chile, California). Fraser (Ceramic Faults and Their Remedies) puts a practical ceiling on raw use: keep to roughly 7-10% of the recipe (European/Turkish sources; American colemanite tolerates somewhat more) or risk 'splutter' - glaze pieces ejecting from the ware as colemanite's ~27%-by-weight water of crystallisation releases too fast, typically 400-800C. Calcium borate frit is chemically equivalent with that water already removed, and is the standard fix.

materials.name: Calcined Kaolin
materials.description: Kaolin fired to remove crystal-bound water. No LOI, no shrinkage, no plasticity. Used to replace raw kaolin when high kaolin content (>20%) causes drying cracks — maintains glaze chemistry without the shrinkage. Refractory, softens around cone 35.

materials.name: Ferro Frit 3269
materials.description: Leadless high-alkali low-calcia frit. High thermal expansion (9.98) makes it useful for crackle glazes — try with ~10% kaolin. Works as partial or full glaze base at cone 06-01. Analysis also carries ~1.5% F.

materials.name: Ferro Frit 3278
materials.description: Leadless high-boron calcia-alkali silicate frit. Elevated Na2O gives high thermal expansion. Recommended for wall tile glazes at cone 08-02. High B2O3 makes it active at low temperatures.

materials.name: Goldart
materials.description: Cedar Heights airfloated plastic stoneware clay from southern Ohio. Wide firing range, excellent working properties; fires light buff at cone 10 reduction. Substitute for Jordan fireclay.

materials.name: Barnard Slip
materials.description: Non-plastic silty iron/manganese clay, long used as an iron source in dark-firing glazes. Fires brown at cone 04 to black by cone 3. High fired shrinkage; messy and staining to handle.

materials.name: Tile #6 Kaolin
materials.description: Air-floated highly plastic kaolin with high green strength — exceptional among North American kaolins. Good for suspending glazes and for throwing bodies. Not suited to casting bodies (relatively impermeable).

materials.name: Ulexite
materials.description: Sodium calcium borate mineral, one of the lowest-melting non-lead ceramic minerals — forms ultra-gloss transparent glass by cone 06. High LOI complicates clear low-fire glazes; use drop-and-hold or thinner application. A component of Gerstley Borate and a common GB replacement.

materials.name: F-4 Feldspar
materials.description: Soda feldspar prized for porcelain due to low iron. Discontinued — Minspar 200 (formerly NC-4) has virtually identical chemistry and is the recommended substitute.

materials.name: G-200 HP Feldspar
materials.description: Successor to the original G-200, with higher potassium. Also discontinued. Blending 7:3 with a soda feldspar approximates original G-200 chemistry.

materials.name: Laguna Borate
materials.description: Formulated Gerstley Borate substitute, delisted by Laguna as of 2023. Chemistry differs enough from GB to cause problems with iron reds, metallics, floating blues, chrome-tin pinks and opalescents. Needs 6-8% bentonite or hectorite for suspension.

materials.name: Sheffield Slip
materials.description: Albany Slip substitute: Sheffield (MA) glacial clay blended with fluxes, designed to duplicate 100% Albany at cone 10 in oxidation or reduction.

materials.name: Fusion Frit F-69
materials.description: Low-expansion magnesium frit with no Na2O/K2O. Base for low-expansion glazes; added to low/mid-fire glazes to solve crazing. Softening point 1700F; listed COE 3.96e-6. May need added CaO or other flux to melt fully.

materials.name: Fusion Frit F-75
materials.description: High-sodium high-expansion low-boron bond frit, very similar to Ferro 3110 (flows slightly more freely, lower surface tension). Used for crackle glazes, concentrated Na2O supply, and clarity in crystalline glazes.

materials.name: Helmer Kaolin
materials.description: Idaho kaolin used primarily for its flashing properties in wood firing. Wet-processed to remove soluble salts and iron. Distributed by Plainsman as 'Troy Clay' (hammermilled ~40 mesh).

materials.name: Newman Red Clay
materials.description: High-temperature red-burning low-plasticity stoneware/fireclay. Staining power beyond what its iron suggests - stays bright red at 50% dilution in oxidation. Usually compounded with ball clay and feldspar.

materials.name: Lincoln 60
materials.description: Dark buff-firing plastic stoneware ('not really a fireclay' despite the name). Gladding McBean sewer-pipe clay from the late 1800s; backbone of West Coast pottery bodies. Vitrifies unglazed by cone 10.

materials.name: Mahavir Potash Feldspar
materials.description: Indian high-grade white-firing potash feldspar, imported by Laguna. Positioned as the G-200/Custer successor: marginally higher K2O and SiO2, slightly lower alumina. Melting temperature ~1220C.
